---
title: Ray Train
description: How to use Axolotl with Ray Train
---

Axolotl supports Ray as a first-class launcher, as an alternative to
`accelerate` for orchestrating training. This is especially useful for
multi-node training: you declare cluster-global resources once and Ray derives
the topology — there are no machine ranks, rendezvous endpoints, or per-node
config files to manage.

Training runs through Ray Train's
[`TorchTrainer`](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/api/doc/ray.train.torch.TorchTrainer.html#ray.train.torch.TorchTrainer).
Install the extra with `pip install axolotl[ray]`.

## Quick start

Describe the run in a [runtime config](runtime-config.qmd) and select the ray
launcher:

```yaml
# cluster.yaml
launcher: ray
ray:
  num_workers: auto    # one worker per available GPU
  resources_per_worker:
    GPU: 1
```

With no `address` set, axolotl uses the cluster brought up by `axolotl ray up`
(or any `ray start` cluster) when one is running, and an isolated local Ray
instance otherwise. Set `address: auto` to require attaching to the most
recently started local cluster, `ray://host:10001` for a specific one, or an
`http(s)://` address for remote Jobs submission (below).

```bash
axolotl train recipe.yaml --runtime cluster.yaml
# or, without a runtime file:
axolotl train recipe.yaml --launcher ray
```

`--launcher ray` alone uses the legacy config keys (`ray_num_workers`, default
1); the runtime file unlocks `num_workers: auto` and the Jobs API flow below.

## Setting up a Ray cluster

A Ray cluster has one _head_ node and any number of worker nodes; training is
launched from the head and scheduled onto workers automatically. If you already
run Ray (KubeRay, the autoscaler, a managed platform), `--launcher ray`
attaches to it and nothing else is needed — see the official
[cluster docs](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/cluster/getting-started.html).

For bare-metal nodes without an existing setup, axolotl can bring the cluster
up itself over passwordless ssh:

```bash
# on the head node; hostfile lists the worker nodes (see examples/runtime/hostfile.example)
axolotl ray up --hostfile hostfile
axolotl ray status        # sanity check: node list, total CPUs/GPUs
axolotl ray down          # tear down head + workers when done
```

`up` records the cluster under `~/.cache/axolotl/`, so `status` and `down`
need no arguments. `down --force` kills only daemons tagged with the cluster's
unique temp dir, never co-tenant Ray clusters.

You can also verify any cluster manually with `ray status` or the
[Ray dashboard](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-observability/getting-started.html).

## Remote submission (Ray Jobs API)

Point `address` at a cluster's dashboard port and axolotl submits the run via
the [Ray Jobs API](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/cluster/running-applications/job-submission/index.html)
instead of running locally — no SSH to the head node required:

```yaml
launcher: ray
ray:
  address: http://head-node:8265
  num_workers: auto
  runtime_env:
    working_dir: .          # uploaded with the job
    excludes: ["outputs/"]
    env_vars:
      HF_HOME: /mnt/shared/hf
```

Logs stream to your terminal until the job finishes; Ctrl-C stops the job
unless `ray.detach: true` is set. Anything not uploaded via `working_dir`
(datasets, deepspeed JSONs referenced by path) must already exist on the
cluster or shared storage.

## Choosing resources

- `num_workers`: `auto` derives the worker count from total cluster resources
  and `resources_per_worker`; an integer pins it exactly.
- `resources_per_worker`: a Ray
  [resource request](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/scheduling/resources.html)
  per worker. To restrict training to a specific GPU type on a mixed cluster:

```yaml
ray:
  resources_per_worker:
    GPU: 1
    accelerator_type:L40S: 0.001
```

## Legacy config keys

The original flags still work and now behave consistently — `use_ray: true` in
the training YAML selects the ray launcher on its own, and conflicting flags
(`--use-ray --launcher torchrun`) error instead of silently ignoring one:

```yaml
use_ray: true
ray_num_workers: 4
resources_per_worker:
    GPU: 1
```

```bash
axolotl train examples/llama-3/lora-1b-ray.yml --use-ray   # deprecated spelling
```

Prefer `launcher: ray` in a runtime file for new setups; CLI flags like
`--ray-num-workers` override runtime-file values when both are given.

## Monitoring

Training progress for any of these flows is visible on the Ray dashboard
(`http://<head>:8265`), including per-node GPU utilization under the Cluster
tab.
